correctness.rationale: For the stated unitary transform, vanishing on the time support S is the kernel condition for its principal minor. Translation acts on this matrix by invertible diagonal factors and a scalar, so sets through the origin suffice. Independently exhausted those sets in bounded batches using the Schur complement of the origin entry and vectorized modular elimination at primitive seventh roots, in reversed field order. By the cyclotomic specialization homomorphism a nonzero residue rules out characteristic-zero singularity. The exact subset determinant recurrence in Z[T]/(T^7−1) returns zero for all 672 remaining six-sets; no smaller candidate remains. At size six the successive modular survivor counts in this run were 14208, 768, 672, 672. The 672 normalized zeros give 5488 sets by marked-point double counting. Every five-point principal block is invertible, forcing rank five and all coordinates nonzero on the nonzero kernel line. Linear similitudes preserve singularity by Galois conjugation; independent enumeration of all 2-by-2 matrices by A^T A=λI found 96 maps. Direct affine images of the three stated representatives produced disjoint classes of sizes 2352, 784, 2352 and exhausted all 5488 sets. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_fourier7.py <fresh-output-directory>; output in /workspace/branches/fourier7_reproduction.txt. This proves a finite standard-dot-product theorem, not an all-prime result.

value.rationale: The standard pairing on the first prime in the complementary residue class is a natural boundary instance of the support-disjointness problem. A complete minimal layer is more informative than another example: it determines precisely what minimum-size cancellation geometries and coefficient freedoms are available, and offers concrete orbit types to test structural conjectures beyond this finite plane.
residual_risks: The classified finite geometry does not by itself generalize to other pairings or primes.
